note: This is what turns the scanner into a continual improvement tool rather than a news feed. Each topic maps a regulatory subject onto the specific parts of the playbook and artefact set that would have to change. Matching is deterministic and case-insensitive. An item may match several topics.

relevance_gate.note: An item must match at least one of these before it is recorded at all. Applied to sources whose filter is set to 'keywords'.

topics.label: Automated decision-making and Articles 22A to 22D
topics.why: The DUAA safeguards regime is the operative legal test for a council deploying ADM. Any change to it flows straight into the DPIA template and the risk-based approval thresholds.

topics.label: Algorithmic transparency reporting
topics.why: ATRS is mandatory for central government and voluntary for local authorities. A change to that voluntary status is the single highest-impact possible change to the toolkit.

topics.label: Agentic AI and autonomous action
topics.why: The agentic amendment set is the newest and least settled part of the playbook, and the Innovation Hub is already deploying agentic AI.

topics.label: Equality, bias and discrimination
topics.why: PSED exposure is the most likely route to a legal challenge against a council AI deployment, and it is assessed through the EIA.

topics.label: AI security and cyber threat
topics.why: Threat guidance changes faster than anything else in the set and the checklist is the artefact that goes stale first.

topics.label: Procurement and third-party assurance
topics.why: Most council AI is bought rather than built, so procurement rules bite before any internal gate does.

topics.label: Management system and assurance standards
topics.why: The playbook claims alignment to ISO/IEC 42001. Revisions to that family are a direct claim-maintenance issue.

topics.label: Shadow AI and acceptable use
topics.why: The AUP is the artefact most read by ordinary staff and the one most exposed to changes in guidance on general-purpose tools.

topics.label: EU AI Act
topics.why: Reference point, not an obligation. A UK local authority is not straightforwardly in scope, so this records the item and tags the topic but deliberately flags NO sections or artefacts for change. Consistent with the scope caveat in the Current State Assessment.

topics.label: Local government specific
topics.why: Sector-specific guidance is more operationally binding on a council than general AI policy is.

topics.label: Maladministration and Ombudsman findings
topics.why: The Ombudsman is where a resident harmed by an automated decision actually ends up, long before any court. A finding against any English council on automated decision-making is the single most useful precedent this scanner could catch.

topics.label: Safeguarding, children's services and adult social care
topics.why: The highest-consequence council AI sits in these services, and statutory guidance here binds practice more tightly than any AI policy does. This is where the AGPI resident-impact weighting has to hold up.

topics.label: Procurement Act 2023 regime
topics.why: Most council AI is bought, so the procurement regime bites before any internal gate. It is also the reason an AI committee cannot absorb the Procurement Board's delegated authority.

topics.label: Freedom of information and disclosure exposure
topics.why: The register and model cards are disclosable. Knowing that changes what goes in them and how supplier confidentiality claims are handled at procurement.

scope: England, single-tier authority. Topics are the frameworks a council is actually judged against, not UK AI policy in general.
